asi0: In a Norwegian study of 554 people aged 18–60, non-surgical treatment, open surgery and minimally invasive surgery gave similar results after one year. The tendon re-ruptured in 6.2% of the non-surgical group and 0.6% of the surgical groups; nerve injury occurred in 0.6% of the non-surgical group, 2.8% after open surgery and 5.2% after minimally invasive surgery. Surgery is considered more often for late presentation (more than 2–3 weeks), re-rupture, the tendon pulling away from the bone and elite athletes. In a 2019 meta-analysis pooling 29 studies, surgery also meant fewer re-ruptures but more of other complications; in studies using early-movement (functional) rehabilitation, the re-rupture rate did not differ between the two groups. The decision is made with your doctor.
